If you are a hand knitter, think of it this way, a larger needle will produce a large stitch, and therefore a more open knitted fabric. Also the weight of the yarn impacts the size of the stitch and the finished appearance of the knitted fabric.<br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/>With the LK-150 you can use a fine yarn- think of a sock weight yarn. or a #1.  Because of the size of the hooks, the distance between the hooks and the setting of the tension dial, you can create very different fabrics  even in plain stockinette knitting.<br><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/>At the opposite end of the spectrum you can use a  medium #4 weight yarn and create a hand knit look.<br><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/>For heavier yarns, you even have the option of knitting over every other needle.<char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><br><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/>Something to consider ... the size of the hook of the needle determines the thickest yarn you can use.  If you try to use a very bulky (or maybe a hand spun yarn) and it doesn't fit in the hooks of the needles, you'll be splitting the yarn and the stitches won't form properly.<br><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><blockquote class="blockquote_style"><i class="fa fa-lightbulb-o fa-2x aria-hidden="true"></i><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><ul class="lightlist" style="list-style:none;"><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><li>Think of the <b>Carriage Stitch/Tension Dial</b> as the hand knitting needle size.<br><br></li><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><li>Think of the <b>Mast Tension Dial</b> as the tension a hand knitter would apply to the yarn with her fingers</li><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></blockquote><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></div><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><div class="col-sm-3 col-xs-12"><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='09'/><figure><img class="img-thumbnail" src="/challenge/images/v2/50/Tension_mast_dial.jpg"><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><figcaption align="center"><br><b>Tension Dial</b></figcaption><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></figure><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></div><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></div><br><br><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/><char code='0d'/><char code='0a'/></string></var><var name='FIELDNAMES'><string>CHALLENGE_ASSIGNID,CHALLENGE_COMPONENTID,HTMLCONTENT</string></var></struct></data></wddxPacket>
